Subject: Renewal health & adoption readout — Q2 usage and ROI

Hi Karthik,

Hope you had a good week. We're kicking off our internal renewal review and I wanted to get a consolidated readout from Redwood on how our Q2 usage maps to expected ROI. A few specific asks:

- Can you confirm total token consumption for our account Apr–Jun? Breakout by generation vs embeddings would be helpful.
- Any latency/throughput incidents that impacted production (we saw two short spikes in May).
- Estimated cost delta if we increase commit by 30% and move two high-throughput endpoints to a dedicated pool.
- A short ROI summary we can share with our CFO for the upcoming renewal meeting.

I've attached our internal usage export (fathomai_Q2_usage_report.csv) and the renewal packet deadline is next Tuesday.

Thanks — look forward to a readout.

— Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, FathomAI
alex.morgan@fathomai.com
(415) 555-0192

Cc: procurement@fathomai.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health & adoption readout — Q2 usage and ROI

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary up front: total token consumption increased 23% QoQ driven by embedding-heavy batch jobs, and the two latency spikes correlate with a third-party networking maintenance window (May 14). We can produce an ROI one-pager; attached a draft (redwood_roirecap_q2.pdf).

Responses inline:
- Token consumption (Apr 1–Jun 30): 12.4M gen tokens, 18.7M embedding tokens (total 31.1M). See attachment and the CSV mapped to our server logs.
- Incidents: two brief latency spikes (May 14 and May 29). Both were <6 min tail latency increases and routed to fallback model variant per your configured routing policy; no dropped requests. We include per-route trace links in the drive.
- Cost delta for +30% commit & two endpoints to dedicated pool: estimated incremental committed cost = $9,800/mo with per-token unit cost reduction that yields ~22% unit price improvement on those endpoints. I put detailed math on page 2 of the ROI PDF.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick call to walk the ROI and the proposed term change (we recommend a 12→18 month shift with staged tranche for dedicated capacity).
2) If you confirm the two endpoints, we'll prepare a dedicated pool sizing sheet and a committed pricing addendum.

I've looped in Grace for SLA credit language and Laura for paperwork/term sheet. Happy to jump on a 30-min slot tomorrow afternoon.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: alex.morgan@fathomai.com, procurement@fathomai.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health & adoption readout — Q2 usage and ROI

Looping in a couple of operational notes for the record:

- SLA/credit: since both incidents were routed to compatible fallbacks and error rate didn't exceed 0.1% across the period, we propose a goodwill credit equivalent to one week of burst credits rather than an SLA payout. If FathomAI prefers a formal SLA amendment for the dedicated pool, we can add a tailored SLA with a 99.95% latency SLO and a financial credit table.
- Dedicated sizing: for the two endpoints you described (high-throughput embeddings + generative webhook), a 2x T4 pool (or one small A100 equivalent) with autoscale to 3 nodes during peak should meet headroom. Grace attached a short sizing worksheet.

I recommend we offer the customer an 18-month term with a staged commit: months 1–6 100% of current commit, months 7–18 a 30% uplift. This reduces upfront risk for them and smooths Redwood's capacity planning.

Grace O'Connor
Director of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

2) Procurement asks: if your team needs Net-30 invoicing and SOC 2 attestation addendum, we can include both in the contract. Laura attached the current term sheet v3 (proposed_term_sheet_v3.docx).
